items.title: Northrop Grumman Awarded $290.6 Million NASA Contract for SMBA Instruments
items.summary: Northrop Grumman has secured a $290.6 million contract from NASA to develop and support Sounder for Microwave-Based Applications (SMBA) instruments for NOAA satellites.
items.content: Northrop Grumman has been awarded a $290.6 million contract by NASA, acting on behalf of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), to provide design, development, production, testing, and mission support for three Sounder for Microwave-Based Applications (SMBA) instruments. These instruments are intended for use on NOAA's Near Earth Orbit Network satellites. The contract is a hybrid agreement incorporating cost-plus-fixed-fee, firm-fixed-price, and time-and-materials structures. The project is scheduled to run from November 23, 2026, through April 1, 2042. NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center is managing the acquisition, while NOAA will own and operate the instruments.

items.title: UnitedHealth Group Faces Market Pressure Following CMS Medicare Advantage Audit Proposal
items.summary: UnitedHealth Group shares experienced significant volatility following a regulatory proposal from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) regarding Medicare Advantage risk-adjustment data validation audits.
items.content: UnitedHealth Group and other major health insurers have faced downward pressure on their stock prices following a proposal by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) to extend risk-adjustment data validation (RADV) audits. The proposal, which allows CMS to recover overpayments dating back to 2018, has created uncertainty regarding the financial impact on Medicare Advantage plans. While some market commentary initially conflated this with changes to the Medicare Advantage "Star Ratings" program, the core issue involves the mechanism used to verify payment accuracy based on member health status. CMS has opened a 60-day public comment period for the proposal, which is scheduled to run through January 19, 2027.

items.content: LightInTheBox Holding Co., Ltd. filed an opposition claim on November 16, 2026, with the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board of the US Patent and Trademark Office. The agency has until January 15, 2027, to respond to the opposition, with potential for a default judgment if it fails to do so.

Zscaler shares rose about 16%, while CrowdStrike is now down 26% from its recent highs. Bleeker lays out both cases. The bull case is that cybersecurity budgets must rise as companies patch systems, with outages at Apple and others as examples. The bear case is that frontier AI models may become the center of cyber defense, which raises questions about what companies like CrowdStrike offer. Expect choppy trading in these shares while investors sort that out.

The S&P 500 was up about 4.5% in midday trading, after news broke that Jensen Huang will return as CEO of NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA). The IT sector gained 8.6%, while financials rose 1.7%, utilities 0.96% and health care 0.9%. Real estate and energy declined. The State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA: SPY) rose about 4.5%. Chips drove the move. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ: SOXX) gained 12.9%, led by NVIDIA, which was up more than 30%. The iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (Cboe: IGV) rose about 4%, so software stocks reacted far less than chip stocks. The GraniteShares 2x Long NVIDIA Daily ETF (NASDAQ: NVDL) jumped 60% but is still down nearly 50% over the past month. NVIDIA traded around $180 before Huang's ouster and hasn't recovered that level. Many stocks bouncing 20% or more today fell 20% or more at the end of last week. Watch whether this is a relief rally or the start of a recovery after the market rotated out of AI and into defensive sectors.
